q: A Fann viscometer reads θ600 = 52 and θ300 = 34. What are the plastic viscosity and yield point?
Why is barite added to a drilling fluid?
options: To build viscosity in fresh water
To reduce filtrate loss in shale
why: Barite (SG ≈ 4.2) is a weighting material. Viscosity and fluid loss are handled by clays and polymers.

q: Which solids-control device removes the coarsest cuttings first?
why: The shaker is the first stage; hydrocyclones and centrifuges then take progressively finer solids.

q: Differential sticking is most likely when…
options: pipe is stationary against a thick filter cake opposite a permeable zone
the hole is washed out in shale
the mud weight is below pore pressure
a key seat forms in a dogleg
why: Overbalance presses stationary pipe into the cake; thick cake and permeable rock make it worse.

q: What is the hydrostatic pressure of 12.0 ppg mud at 10,000 ft TVD?
Seismic reflections are produced by contrasts in…
why: Reflection strength depends on the change in ρV between layers.

q: A reflector is at 2.0 s two-way time with an average velocity of 3,000 m/s. How deep is it?
Which wave cannot travel through liquids?
why: Liquids have no shear strength, so shear waves cannot travel through them.

q: What is the purpose of migration in seismic processing?
options: Move dipping events to their true subsurface positions
why: Migration repositions reflections and collapses diffractions.

q: With V = 3,000 m/s and a dominant frequency of 30 Hz, the approximate vertical resolution (λ/4) is…
Which is a stratigraphic trap?
options: A sandstone that pinches out into shale
why: Stratigraphic traps come from changes in rock type, not from deformation.

q: The oil window is roughly…
why: Below it the rock is immature; above it the source rock mainly generates gas.

q: Which rock most often acts as a seal?
why: A seal needs very low permeability.

q: Kerogen is…
options: insoluble organic matter that generates hydrocarbons when heated
why: Kerogen is the solid organic precursor of oil and gas.

q: Normal hydrostatic pressure gradient for saline formation water is about…
why: Fresh water is 0.433 psi/ft; typical brines are about 0.465 psi/ft.

q: In a clean gas sand, the density and neutron porosity logs typically show…
options: density porosity higher than neutron porosity (crossover)
why: Gas lowers hydrogen index (neutron reads low) and bulk density (density porosity reads high).

q: A sandstone has ρb = 2.32 g/cc, ρma = 2.65 and ρf = 1.0. What is the density porosity?
With a = 1, m = n = 2, Rw = 0.05 Ω·m, φ = 0.20 and Rt = 20 Ω·m, what is Sw?
High gamma ray readings usually indicate…
why: Clays concentrate potassium, thorium and uranium.

q: Which log is most useful for distinguishing hydrocarbons from salt water in a porous zone?
why: Hydrocarbons don't conduct electricity, so they raise resistivity compared with salt water.

q: A well kicks at 10,000 ft TVD with 10.0 ppg mud; SIDPP = 520 psi. What is the kill mud weight?
Which is NOT a positive kick indicator?
options: Decrease in rate of penetration in a hard stringer
why: A drilling break (sudden increase in ROP) is a warning sign; a slowdown is not.

q: The wait and weight method kills the well in…
why: Kill mud is pumped while the influx is circulated out, all in one circulation.

q: Hydrostatic pressure depends on…
why: Only the vertical height of the fluid column matters.

q: A leak-off test is performed to determine…
options: the fracture gradient below the casing shoe
why: It sets the upper bound of the mud weight window for the next hole section.

q: Positive skin indicates…
why: Positive skin means an extra pressure drop near the well; stimulation gives negative skin.

q: A gravel pack is used mainly for…
why: The sized gravel holds back formation sand behind a screen.

q: Matrix acidizing is performed…
why: The aim is to treat the near-wellbore matrix without fracturing it.

q: Which device isolates the tubing–casing annulus above the reservoir?
why: A packer seals the annulus.

q: What does a subsurface safety valve do?
options: Shuts in the well automatically if surface control is lost
why: It is a fail-safe barrier below the tree.

q: Which intervention method cannot transmit electrical data?
why: Slickline is a solid single wire with no conductor.

q: Coiled tubing is often preferred for cleanouts because it…
options: can circulate fluid continuously while running into a live well
why: It runs in continuously without connections and lets fluid circulate the whole time.

q: What is the purpose of plug and abandonment?
options: Permanently isolate zones and protect groundwater at end of life
why: P&A seals a well permanently.

q: What is the capacity of 2.992-in ID tubing?
Snubbing means…
options: running pipe into a well under pressure
killing a well with heavy brine
why: Hydraulic jacks push the pipe in against the well pressure.

q: Polymer flooding mainly improves…
why: Polymer thickens the water, so the mobility ratio falls.

q: A mobility ratio greater than 1 means…
why: The displacing fluid moves more easily than the oil, so it channels through it.

q: Surfactant flooding works mainly by…
why: Lower IFT raises the capillary number and releases trapped oil.

q: Above the minimum miscibility pressure, injected CO2 and oil…
why: Miscibility removes the interface between gas and oil.

q: If E_D = 0.6, E_A = 0.7 and E_V = 0.8, the overall recovery efficiency is…
A crude has specific gravity 0.876. Its API gravity is about…
A drillstem test is…
options: a temporary completion using the drillstring to flow and test a zone
why: A DST flows the zone, records pressures and takes samples.

q: The absolute open flow of a gas well is the rate at…
why: AOF is a theoretical maximum used to compare wells.

q: The best fluid sample for PVT, if the reservoir is above its saturation pressure, is…
why: It captures the reservoir fluid before gas comes out of solution.

q: A well makes 800 bbl oil and 200 bbl water per day. Water cut is…
On a log-log derivative plot, infinite-acting radial flow appears as…
why: Radial flow gives a constant derivative; unit slope is wellbore storage.

q: A buildup gives semilog slope m = 50 psi/cycle, q = 500 STB/d, B = 1.2, μ = 1 cp, h = 50 ft. What is k?
A falloff test is run on…
why: Injection stops and the pressure decline is analyzed.

q: Wellbore storage affects…
why: Fluid in the wellbore compresses or expands at first and masks the reservoir's response.

q: What does extrapolating a Horner plot to a time ratio of 1 give?
why: p* is used to estimate average reservoir pressure.

q: Area 640 acres, h = 30 ft, φ = 0.20, Swi = 0.25, Boi = 1.2 rb/STB. What is OOIP?
A variogram describes…
options: how dissimilarity between samples grows with distance
why: It is the spatial-correlation model used in kriging.

q: Which drive mechanism usually gives the highest oil recovery?
why: Water drive commonly gives about 35–60%; solution gas drive about 5–30%.

q: A P90 estimate means…
options: 90% chance the true value is at least this
90% chance the true value is less than this
why: P90 is the low, conservative case.

q: History matching is…
options: tuning a simulation model to reproduce past production and pressure
why: A matched model can then be used to forecast.

q: A spinner flowmeter measures…
why: Spinner rotation speed is roughly proportional to fluid velocity.

q: Holdup is different from phase cut because of…
why: Lighter phases move faster, so they occupy less of the pipe than their share of the flow.

q: Oil 0.8 g/cc, water 1.0 g/cc, measured mixture density 0.95 g/cc. Water holdup is…
A cement bond log evaluates…
why: Well-bonded pipe damps the acoustic signal.

q: Which cased-hole log can estimate water saturation behind casing?
why: The capture cross section (sigma) separates salt water from hydrocarbons.

q: A three-phase separator separates…
why: Each phase leaves through its own outlet.

q: Glycol dehydration removes…
why: TEG absorbs water and is regenerated by heating.

q: Hydrates are most likely at…
options: high pressure and low temperature with free water
why: Hydrates need water, light gas, high pressure and low temperature.

q: Amine units are used for…
why: Amine treating is gas sweetening.

q: A LACT unit is used for…
why: It measures, samples and checks oil quality when ownership changes.

q: A well produces 400 STB/d with p̄r = 3,000 psi and pwf = 2,000 psi. What is PI?
In nodal analysis, the operating rate is where…
options: the inflow (IPR) curve meets the outflow curve
why: At that point the pressure the reservoir delivers equals the pressure the tubing needs.

q: Which lift method is usually best for very high liquid rates?
why: ESPs handle thousands of bbl/d.

q: Exponential decline corresponds to Arps b = …
why: b = 0 is exponential, 0 < b < 1 hyperbolic, b = 1 harmonic.

q: Liquid loading occurs in…
options: gas wells with low gas velocity
why: The gas can't carry the liquids up, so they accumulate and choke the well.

q: Which property is MOST important to rank a shale source-rock reservoir?
why: TOC measures the organic richness that generates and stores gas.

q: Shale gas is stored as…
options: free gas in pores and adsorbed gas on organic matter
why: Both mechanisms contribute; the Langmuir isotherm describes the adsorbed part.

q: Why are horizontal wells with multistage fractures used in shale?
options: Ultra-low permeability needs huge contact area
why: Nanodarcy rock only flows at useful rates through a large fractured contact area.

q: Vitrinite reflectance Ro ≈ 1.5% suggests the source rock is in the…
why: About 0.6–1.3% is the oil window; above about 1.3% generates gas.

q: Microseismic monitoring is used to…
why: It locates the small events created as fractures grow.

q: SCADA systems are used for…
options: remote monitoring and control of field equipment
why: Supervisory control and data acquisition.

q: WITSML is a standard for exchanging…
why: It is an XML standard for well and drilling data.

q: A digital twin is…
options: a live virtual model of a physical asset
a second well on a pad
why: It is updated with real data to monitor the asset and test changes.

q: DTS measures…
why: It gives a temperature profile along the whole fiber.

q: Predictive maintenance schedules work based on…
why: It uses data to act before a failure happens.

q: Underbalanced perforating helps because…
options: the inflow surge cleans debris from tunnels
it increases charge penetration in steel
why: Reservoir pressure flushes crushed rock and debris out of the tunnels.

q: A 20-ft interval shot at 6 spf has how many perforations?
Which charge type is preferred for gravel packing?
why: Large holes reduce pressure drop through the gravel-filled tunnels.

q: Depth control before perforating is done with…
why: The tool's depth is tied to the open-hole log depth.

q: TCP stands for…
why: Guns run on tubing.

q: A project with NPV > 0 at 10% means…
why: A positive NPV at rate i means IRR is above i.

q: Proved reserves (1P) have at least…
options: 90% probability of being met or exceeded
why: In probabilistic terms 1P is the P90 estimate.

q: In a production sharing contract, cost oil is…
options: the share of production that repays the contractor's costs
why: What remains after cost oil is profit oil, which is split with the government.

q: How many BOE is 12 MMscf of gas, at 6,000 scf/BOE?
Midstream covers…
why: It sits between upstream and downstream.

q: Heavy oil is usually defined as below about…
why: Below about 10 °API is extra-heavy.

q: SAGD uses…
options: a horizontal injector above a horizontal producer
why: Steam rises from the upper well; heated bitumen drains by gravity to the lower one.

q: Why are thermal methods effective for heavy oil?
why: Heavy oil viscosity can drop by orders of magnitude when heated.

q: A lower steam-oil ratio means…
why: Less steam is needed per barrel produced.

q: CHOPS stands for…
options: cold heavy oil production with sand
why: Sand is produced deliberately and the wells run without heat.

q: One barrel equals…
US standard conditions are…
why: Oilfield volumes in scf and STB use 60 °F and 14.696 psia.

q: Absolute pressure equals gauge pressure plus…
why: psia = psig + 14.7.

q: A wildcat well is…
options: an exploration well in an unproven area
why: It tests an area with no previous discovery.

q: To spud a well means to…
why: The spud date is the start of drilling.
